title: Probing the Error-Mitigation Threshold with Matrix Product States
authors: Jia-Yao Zhao, Zhi-Yuan Wei, Michael J. Gullans
abstract: Quantum error mitigation relies on accurate noise characterization, but mismatches between the actual and characterized noise can be amplified and drive a sharp threshold between successful and failed mitigation. In random circuits, this threshold maps onto a random-field Ising transition, but previous exact numerics were limited to small one-dimensional and all-to-all systems, leaving explicit two-dimensional architectures unresolved. We develop a fixed-bond-dimension matrix-product-state method for the replicated transfer dynamics that extends threshold calculations beyond exact propagation while retaining the finite-size signatures of the transition. At system sizes beyond previous exact studies, we recover the predicted absence of a threshold for quenched disorder in 1D, obtain a sharper annealed all-to-all critical point, and resolve architecture-dependent finite-depth thresholds in 2D square and heavy-hex circuits. These results establish replicated tensor-network dynamics as a practical tool for probing error-mitigation thresholds in large and higher-dimensional noisy circuits.
summary: This work develops a novel Matrix Product State (MPS) technique to probe the error-mitigation threshold in large, high-dimensional quantum circuits. By mapping the problem to a replicated statistical model, the authors overcome previous computational limitations to precisely determine critical thresholds for 2D lattices. This establishes replicated tensor-network dynamics as a practical tool for assessing quantum hardware noise resilience.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately determining the error-mitigation threshold in quantum circuits when noise characterization is imperfect.
main_result: The authors successfully extended threshold calculations to large and higher-dimensional noisy circuits (2D square and heavy-hex) by developing a fixed-bond-dimension MPS method.
method: They map the circuit dynamics to a replicated transfer process modeled as a Random-Field Ising Model, which is then simulated using a fixed-bond-dimension Matrix Product State (MPS) approach.
model_or_system: The system is a noisy random circuit on qubits, whose dynamics are analyzed via a two-replica statistical model. The analysis covers various geometries: 1D, all-to-all, 2D square, and 2D heavy-hex lattices.
key_observables: Rényi-2 Entropy ($S_a$) and two-point mutual information ($I_{ab}$) are used as primary diagnostics to locate the phase transition threshold.
important_parameters:
The critical disorder strength ($\sigma_c/ ar{q}$) and the critical exponent ($
u$) are the key extracted parameters, alongside the bond dimension ($\chi$) and circuit depth ($t$).
main_assumptions: The core approximation is the use of a fixed-bond-dimension MPS truncation ($\chi$) to compress the high-dimensional replicated dynamics, allowing study beyond exact propagation limits.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate the phase diagram separating success/failure regimes, show entanglement evolution ($S_a$) for different disorder types, and present finite-size scaling collapses for determining $\sigma_c/ ar{q}$ and $

paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the necessary transfer rules for the two-replica model, implements the evolution using MPS/TEBD, and then applies finite-size scaling analysis to extract critical parameters for different lattice geometries.
why_interesting: The application of tensor networks (MPS) to study non-equilibrium quantum error correction thresholds provides a powerful, scalable computational tool for characterizing noise robustness in complex quantum hardware architectures.
